problem_statement: davidfaure/horizontal-parallax-gallery-codrops is a Vite + WebGL/DOM "Horizontal Parallax Gallery" Codrops demo: a full-viewport black stage with a Codrops frame header (title, Tutorial/All demos/GitHub links, #scroll/#three.js/#webgl tags, and a 2D/DOM ↔ WebGL route switch) and a horizontally-scrolling parallax track of ten local WebP portrait frames (1.webp–10.webp). Above the track sits the gallery's own "Portrait finder": a tone filter bar (All / Warm / Cool / Neon pills, plus a live "Showing N of 10 · <tone>" readout) that filters the ten frames by colour tone and re-renders the track. The same finder rides both the 2D/DOM route (index.html) and the WebGL route (index2.html). Three defects shipped together and must be repaired: (1) MOBILE OVERFLOW — on a 390px phone the finder's pill row is laid out at a fixed 760px with flex-wrap:nowrap, so the four pills cannot fit and push the document width past the viewport, leaving a dead horizontal gutter (the parallax track itself is fine, it is clipped inside its own overflow-hidden wrapper). (2) BROKEN FINDER LAYOUT — a mis-styled variant shingles the pills over each other with negative margins and renders the active pill and readout in near-black on the black bar (illegible), so a designer cannot read the tones or the count. (3) STALE FILTER — a variant wires the click to only flip the active pill: the readout and the filtered track are snapshotted once at load and never recompute, so clicking "Warm" leaves "Showing 10 of 10 · All tones" frozen and all ten frames on screen. Repair the finder so: the mobile home page (and the WebGL route) no longer scroll horizontally with the pill row reflowing within the viewport (not clipped by overflow-x:hidden); the bar is legible with a high-contrast active pill and readable readout; the tone-filter interaction stays wired so clicking a tone control re-filters the track and rewrites the readout to "Showing N of 10 · <tone>" live; and the finder is present on BOTH the 2D/DOM and WebGL routes. The finder's tone controls drive the same ten frames that the WebGL/3D route renders on its full-viewport canvas stage, so the interaction must behave identically across routes. Keep the ten-frame parallax gallery, the Codrops frame/nav, the route switch, and the desktop/tablet layout intact.
required_content: The mobile home page (390px) no longer scrolls horizontally: the Portrait finder pill row reflows within the viewport so documentElement scrollWidth stays within the 390px viewport beyond a small tolerance.
The WebGL route (index2.html) also carries the Portrait finder bar and is overflow-free; the finder is present on BOTH the 2D/DOM and WebGL routes.
The Portrait finder bar is legible: pills do not overlap, and the active pill and the 'Showing N of 10' readout are high-contrast (not near-black on the black bar).

Clicking a tone pill (e.g. Warm) re-filters the parallax track to that tone and rewrites the readout live to 'Showing 3 of 10 · Warm'; the count and shown frames track the clicked tone rather than a frozen snapshot.
The ten-frame horizontal-parallax gallery, the Codrops frame header, the #scroll/#three.js/#webgl tags, and the 2D/DOM ↔ WebGL route switch remain intact and reachable.
Desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts are unchanged and remain overflow-free.
No new runtime console errors or failed network requests are introduced.
design_constraints: Preserve the Codrops black-on-white monospace visual system: full-viewport black stage, thin 1px borders, rounded pills, ui-monospace type, and the frame header grid.
Do not remove or restructure the horizontal-parallax gallery track, the WebGL route, the TypeScript parallax engine, the shaders, or the ten local WebP assets.
Fix the overflow at the layout level (let the finder pill row wrap / use flexible pill sizing); do NOT paper over it with a blanket overflow-x:hidden on html/body or the row.

The Portrait finder is the gallery's own filter feature: it must live above the track on every route, filter the frames by tone, and keep its live 'Showing N of 10 · <tone>' readout in sync with the clicked pill (the tone-filter interaction and its controls must stay wired).

Keep the active-pill and readout contrast legible against the black bar (light-on-dark button-style pills), preserve the card-like frame spacing and monospace typography, and keep the four tone pills readable and non-overlapping.
Keep the layout responsive: the mobile pill row must reflow within the viewport and the visual style of the bar must match the surrounding image gallery chrome.
state_constraints: desktop_initial and desktop_finder capture the 1440px home page: black gallery stage, Codrops frame header, the ten-frame parallax track, and the Portrait finder bar with four tone pills in a single legible row — no horizontal overflow.
tablet_initial captures the 834px home page, also overflow-free.
mobile_initial and mobile_finder capture the 390px home page where the finder pill row must reflow within the viewport with no horizontal overflow.
desktop_warm_filter and mobile_warm_filter capture the state AFTER clicking the 'Warm' tone pill: the parallax track shows only the warm-toned frames and the readout reads 'Showing 3 of 10 · Warm'.
desktop_webgl and mobile_webgl capture the WebGL route (index2.html), which carries the same Portrait finder bar (cross-route presence) over the WebGL stage.

change_completion: Clicking a tone pill re-filters the parallax track and updates the 'Showing N of 10 · <tone>' readout live to match the clicked tone.
The Portrait finder is present above the track on BOTH the 2D/DOM (index.html) and WebGL (index2.html) routes.
design_consistency: The finder keeps the Codrops black-on-white monospace system with legible, non-overlapping pills and a high-contrast active pill and readout.
The active pill and readout are readable against the black bar (no near-black-on-black contrast failure).
regression: The ten-frame parallax gallery, WebGL route, parallax engine, shaders, and Codrops frame/nav remain intact and reachable.
No new runtime console errors or failed network requests are introduced.
responsive: The mobile (390px) home page and WebGL route no longer scroll horizontally; the finder pill row reflows within the viewport.
Desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts are unchanged and overflow-free.

author_notes: Native gallery lever for the davidfaure horizontal-parallax-gallery-codrops Codrops demo: the gallery's own Portrait finder tone filter bar sits above the ten-frame WebP parallax track and filters the portrait frames (Warm / Cool / Neon) with a live 'Showing N of 10' count. The four leg-varying files are css/portrait-finder.css (mobile pill-row overflow + the illegible shingled-pill layout defect), src/portrait-finder.ts (correct live filter vs the stale frozen-snapshot wiring), index2.html (finder presence on the WebGL route), and the shared index.html markup. Reference filters correctly, is legible and reflows on mobile, and carries the finder on both routes. Assets: the ten local WebP portrait frames 1.webp–10.webp drive the tone filter. Design keywords: gallery, portrait, tone filter, parallax, responsive layout.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Vite + WebGL/DOM Codrops horizontal-parallax gallery with ten local WebP portrait frames, a 2D/DOM and WebGL route, and a compact black-on-white monospace visual system; the gallery naturally hosts a tone filter bar above its track (the Portrait finder), giving a native gallery-filter lever — repair the mobile overflow, the illegible shingled-pill layout, and the stale-snapshot filter wiring, with cross-route presence on the DOM and WebGL routes and the intentional horizontal-scroll track scoped out of the overflow measurement.
metadata.bug_report: On a 390px phone the gallery home page scrolls sideways: the Portrait finder's tone-pill row runs off the right edge. The pills are also unreadable (overlapping, near-black on black) and clicking a tone does nothing to the count or the frames. The finder is also missing on the WebGL route.
